teaser: Officer Rusk broke the rule he had made himself and wrote an adult wording into the green journal: the flowering asking again, blood over the roots until the plant is still. The plant answered him for the first time in the book's history, though not with anything a book can hear — the whole crown and the open flower turned down to the wet soil under his hand — and the third morning came with both his eyes in his face, because the line he had written was finished before he cut. Now the farm owns a page it can always pay, the sign over the shelf has not changed by a stroke, and the flower that looked at the lamps for four days is looking at the ground and will not look up.

options.label: Read the sign in the trench
options.prompt: Continue the story: have Bea read the whole name sign to the plant with the crown lamps moved down to the trench where the flower is now looking, and show what the three hooks ask once the plant has been fed at the roots.

options.label: Let the gauge move
options.prompt: Continue the story: let the farm live a week on lines that cannot fail, and show what happens when the air gauge of the work ring finally moves and nobody has read the leaves.

options.label: Send Bea to Iven
options.prompt: Continue the story: send Bea down the spine alone, as Iven asked, without the doctor and without the green journal, and show what the old Reader draws from the last flowering and what he says about the name the farm paid with.
